title: Hand-place three SMD parts on their pads to IPC Class 3, tantalum band on the + pad
instruction: Place the three parts on the circuit board, each on the pair of silver pads that matches its size (pads a little wider than the part and reaching just past both of its ends): square to its pads and centred on them, with neither end sticking out past a pad. The tantalum capacitor, the largest part, goes with its dark band on the + pad, the one with the small white square (the + mark) beside it.
context: Electronics assemblers and rework technicians (O*NET 51-2022.00) hand-place surface-mount parts on their pads when building prototypes and repairing boards, and the result is judged by IPC-A-610, Acceptability of Electronic Assemblies. For a chip part, end overhang (a termination past the outer end of its pad) is not allowed in any class, and side overhang (a termination past the side of its pad) may be up to half the part's width for Class 1 and 2 products but only a quarter of it for Class 3, high-reliability electronics such as medical and aerospace equipment. A polarised tantalum capacitor placed the wrong way round fails short when the board is powered, a defect in every class.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Electronics rework at 8 times real size. Fixed to the table: (1) Circuit board: green glass-epoxy, 150 mm (x) by 220 mm (y), 4 mm thick, centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0. (2) Three footprints on it, each a pair of flat tinned-copper pads (silver, 1 mm thick) in line along x, centred on x 30.0 cm: the resistor's at y +6.5 cm (pads 18 mm along x by 29 mm, their centres 22 mm either side of x 30.0 cm, so each pad spans 13-31 mm from it), the ceramic capacitor's at y 0 (pads 16 x 24 mm, centres 11 mm either side, spanning 3-19 mm) and the tantalum capacitor's at y -6.5 cm (pads 18 x 38 mm, centres 26 mm either side, spanning 17-35 mm). Each footprint's pads are 2 mm wider on each side than its part and reach 6 mm past each of its ends. The tantalum footprint's far pad (+x, centred at x 32.6 cm) is its + pad: a white plastic square, 8 x 8 mm and 1 mm thick (the + mark), is on the board beside it, centred at x 32.6 cm, y -9.5 cm. (3) Two antistatic mats, dark grey rubber, 90 mm (x) by 130 mm (y), 3 mm thick, centred at x 20.0 cm, y +24.0 cm (left) and y -24.0 cm (right). Loose, each a solid plastic block (1.1-1.45 g/cm3) lying flat on a mat with its long side along y: (4) R1, a 2512 chip resistor: 50 mm long, 25 mm wide, 20 mm tall, 30 g, a black body with silver end caps (its terminations: aluminium foil) over the last 8 mm of each end, round all four long faces; on the left mat, centred at x 20.0 cm, y +21.5 cm. (5) C1, a 1210 ceramic chip capacitor: 26 mm long, 20 mm wide, 20 mm tall, 15 g, a tan body with silver end caps (aluminium foil) over the last 6 mm of each end, round all four long faces (it is square in section); on the left mat, centred at x 20.0 cm, y +26.5 cm. (6) T1, a D-case (7343) moulded tantalum capacitor: 58 mm long, 34 mm wide, 24 mm tall, 50 g, an amber body standing on two aluminium termination plates (silver) under its ends (8 mm long, 1 mm thick: bottom-only terminations), with a dark brown band, 10 mm wide, across its top at its + end; on the right mat, centred at x 20.0 cm, y -24.0 cm, its band end toward +y. The resistor is taller than a real one scaled up (20 mm, not 5 mm) so a gripper can hold it. Each footprint is the one whose pads are 2 mm wider than its own part on each side and reach 6 mm past its ends; no other pair fits a part that way. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the parts' poses (in a real trial: a photo from straight above and a ruler). A part's outline is its shadow seen from straight above; a termination is the last 8 mm of R1's or T1's length at an end (T1's silver plates lie under them) or the last 6 mm of C1's, over the part's full width. 'At rest': neither end of the part moved more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s. A part counts only if, at rest, it lies on its own footprint (the one the setup names for it): flat (tilted 5 degrees or less from lying on a face: R1 on either broad face; C1, square in section with its end caps round all four long faces, on any of them; T1 band face up) with its lowest point within 2 mm of the pads' top; its long axis within 10 degrees of x seen from above; with no end overhang (no point of its outline past the line of either pad's outer end); and, for T1, its band at the + pad's end. Side overhang is how far a termination's outline reaches past the side of its pad (along y, across the footprint's axis), taken at the worse of the part's two terminations. IPC's limit is a share of the part's width or of the pad's, whichever is less; these pads are wider than their parts, so the part's width governs. A counting part scores 1/3 if its side overhang is at most 25% of its width (Class 3: 6.25 mm for R1, 5 mm for C1, 8.5 mm for T1), 1/6 if more than 25% and at most 50% (Classes 1-2 only: 12.5, 10 and 17 mm), and 0 if more. Square and centred along its axis, a part reaches those limits when its centre is 8.25 and 14.5 mm (R1), 7 and 12 mm (C1) or 10.5 and 19 mm (T1) to one side of its footprint's centre line; it may be up to 6 mm off along the axis before an end overhangs. So a part scores 0 if it is on another part's footprint (R1 would fit T1's pads), on top of another part, on its side (R1, T1) or an end, upside down (T1), held more than 2 mm above its pads, still moving, or off the board. Score 0 for the whole trial if at the end any part is off the table (its lowest point more than 5 cm below the table top), or T1 lies on its own pads reversed: flat and band face up with its lowest point within 2 mm of the pads' top, its long axis within 10 degrees of x, its centre within the rectangle its two pads span, and its band at the - pad's end (a reversed tantalum fails short at power-up). Otherwise the score is the sum of the three parts' scores. Possible scores: 0, 0.17, 0.33, 0.5, 0.67, 0.83, 1.0 (for example 0.5 is one part Class 3 and one Class 2, or all three Class 2; 0.83 is two Class 3 and one Class 2). Success is 1.0 (all three Class 3), held at rest for 2.5 s. The scorer sees only the parts, not the grippers: a part held still on its pads counts as placed.
fidelity: Parts and pads are 8 times real size, the resistor 20 mm tall, not 5 mm, so a gripper can hold it; its top is unmarked, so either broad face up counts (a real one goes element up). No solder paste or reflow: nothing holds or self-centres a part, so it is judged as if soldered where it lies. IPC-A-610's chip limits are applied to the moulded tantalum, its terminations full width. Each part is one rigid body of boxes, default friction. The scorer reads only the parts, not the grippers.
reset_notes: Put R1 and C1 back on the left mat (centred at x 20.0 cm, y +21.5 cm and y +26.5 cm) and T1 on the right mat (x 20.0 cm, y -24.0 cm), each flat with its long side along y and T1's band toward +y. Nothing is consumed.
